title: Aperiodic Morphogenesis: Quasicrystalline Reaction-Diffusion
thesis: This project explores the generative fusion of quasicrystalline structural order with reaction-diffusion dynamics, yielding novel forms that manifest complex, aperiodic growth patterns on fixed, geometrically constrained scaffolds.

items.title: Penrose Rhombus Cellular Automata
items.basis: The rigid, aperiodic geometry of Penrose P2 rhombi acts as a fixed lattice, while reaction-diffusion rules determine the filling and evolution of these cells. The 'rules' are not standard cellular automata, but rather emergent behaviors of substrate/inhibitor fields.
items.prompt: Generate a canvas filled with 6-12 distinct glyphs. Each glyph is a Penrose P2 tiling pattern where the rhombi are filled with a reaction-diffusion pattern resembling Turing spots or spirals. The quasicrystalline edges of the rhombi should appear sharp, while the internal patterns exhibit broad, flat 2D shapes in pure black on white. No gray, gradients, or textures. Focus on the interplay between the rigid aperiodic tiling and the organic growth within.
items.why_weird: This hybrid forces an inherently continuous, emergent process (reaction-diffusion) to conform to a discrete, non-repeating geometric system (Penrose tiling), creating a visual tension between growth and constraint.
items.fusion_logic: The quasicrystal provides the fixed, forbidden symmetry scaffold (5-fold and 10-fold) where reaction-diffusion patterns are seeded and constrained. The reaction-diffusion model dictates the localized pattern formation and spread within the defined quasicrystalline regions, leading to complex, non-uniform filling.

source_dna.quasicrystals: Utilizes the Penrose P2 tiling (rhombus tiles) as the fundamental aperiodic geometric framework, imposing 5-fold and 10-fold symmetry constraints on pattern propagation.
source_dna.reaction_diffusion: Applies Gray-Scott model dynamics (or similar) to generate localized, self-organizing patterns (e.g., spots, spirals) that grow and interact within the quasicrystalline regions.

items.title: Ammann-Beenker Octagonal Growth Fronts
items.basis: The 8-fold symmetry of the Ammann-Beenker tiling dictates directional growth fronts for reaction-diffusion systems. The diffusion rates or reaction parameters are modulated by the local orientation relative to the tiling axes.
items.prompt: Create 6-12 unique glyphs. Each glyph displays an Ammann-Beenker octagonal tiling skeleton. Within the spaces defined by this skeleton, reaction-diffusion patterns form, appearing as broad, flat black shapes. These patterns should exhibit directional growth, biased by the 8-fold symmetry axes of the underlying tiling, creating a sense of controlled expansion or fragmentation. Pure 2D silhouettes, black on white.
items.why_weird: The inherent orientational order of the Ammann-Beenker tiling directly influences the anisotropic spread of reaction-diffusion patterns, making the diffusion itself 'aware' of the quasicrystalline structure's symmetry.
items.fusion_logic: The Ammann-Beenker tiling's 8-fold symmetry is used to bias the local diffusion coefficients or reaction rates in the reaction-diffusion simulation. This causes patterns to expand preferentially along certain directions, forming sharp, directional fronts that respect the quasicrystalline axes.

source_dna.quasicrystals: Leverages the Ammann-Beenker tiling's 8-fold symmetry to define anisotropic growth conditions for emergent patterns.
source_dna.reaction_diffusion: The reaction-diffusion system's spatial dynamics are altered, producing anisotropic pattern formation and growth controlled by the local quasicrystalline orientation.

items.title: Stampfli Dodecagonal Halos
items.basis: The 12-fold symmetry of the Stampfli dodecagonal tiling serves as a template for the outward propagation of reaction-diffusion 'halos' or wave-like structures, emanating from specific points or regions within the tiling.
items.prompt: Design 8-10 distinct glyphs. Each glyph features the structural elements of a Stampfli dodecagonal tiling. Concentric, open-centered halos of reaction-diffusion patterns (broad black bands) should be visible, seemingly expanding outwards from vertices or intersections of the tiling. The halos must be flat, 2D, and possess the 12-fold rotational symmetry of the base tiling. Black shapes on a white background.
items.why_weird: This design translates the quasiperiodic symmetry of the tiling into the morphology of diffusion-driven patterns, making the 'halos' intrinsically non-repeating yet highly symmetrical.
items.fusion_logic: The reaction-diffusion simulation is parameterized such that it generates expanding wave-fronts or 'halos'. The dodecagonal quasicrystal structure acts as a guide, influencing the phase and amplitude of these halos at different points, causing them to appear with 12-fold symmetry and open centers.

source_dna.quasicrystals: Employs the Stampfli dodecagonal tiling as a structural and symmetry guide for the spatial distribution and shape of diffusion patterns.
source_dna.reaction_diffusion: Generates self-propagating wave-like patterns (halos) whose structure and expansion are modulated by the 12-fold symmetry of the quasicrystal scaffold.

items.title: Robinson Tiling Hierarchical Patterns
items.basis: The self-similar, hierarchical nature of the Robinson tiling is used to recursively seed reaction-diffusion patterns at multiple scales. Larger 'tiles' contain smaller, similar sub-patterns of reaction-diffusion activity.
items.prompt: Illustrate 6-12 independent glyphs. Each glyph is based on the Robinson tiling's square-based hierarchy. Within the squares and sub-squares of the tiling, reaction-diffusion patterns manifest as solid black forms. These patterns should recursively appear at smaller scales, mirroring the self-similar tiling structure, creating fractal-like complexity within the broad, flat 2D silhouette style.
items.why_weird: This combines recursive geometric construction with emergent pattern formation, creating a visual echo of the tiling's self-similarity in the reaction-diffusion process itself.
items.fusion_logic: The inflation rules and hierarchical subdivision of the Robinson tiling are used to define locations and initial conditions for reaction-diffusion simulations at multiple scales. This forces the reaction-diffusion patterns to inherit and express the self-similar, recursive structure of the quasicrystal.

source_dna.quasicrystals: Utilizes the hierarchical and self-similar substitution rules of the Robinson tiling to define seeding points and structural organization for reaction-diffusion.
source_dna.reaction_diffusion: Generates patterns that recursively emerge at different scales, mirroring the self-similarity of the Robinson tiling, creating fractal-like complexity in the growth.

items.title: Pinwheel Tiling Inverted Halos
items.basis: The unique vertex configuration of the Pinwheel tiling, where edges meet at various angles, creates localized 'singularities' where reaction-diffusion patterns appear as inverted halos or voids.
items.prompt: Generate 7-10 unique glyphs. Each glyph is an arrangement based on the Pinwheel tiling. At the points where the tiling edges converge in specific configurations, reaction-diffusion processes manifest as hollow, open-centered shapes (inverted halos) of pure black, surrounded by a void. The exterior of these patterns should be flat black, forming broad silhouettes with strong negative space. Black on white, 2D.
items.why_weird: The Pinwheel tiling's peculiar vertex structure leads to reaction-diffusion 'holes' or voids rather than filled patterns, inverting the typical growth paradigm.
items.fusion_logic: The specific angles and connections at the vertices of the Pinwheel tiling are used to define areas where reaction-diffusion parameters are set to suppress pattern formation, creating voids or negative space ('inverted halos') within the overall structure.

source_dna.quasicrystals: Employs the vertex geometry and edge configurations of the Pinwheel tiling to define locations of pattern suppression or void formation.
source_dna.reaction_diffusion: Generates 'inverted halos' or voids by configuring reaction-diffusion parameters to prevent pattern formation at specific points dictated by the Pinwheel tiling's structure.

items.title: Trilobite-Sphinx Symmetry Breaking
items.basis: The paired nature of the Trilobite-Sphinx tiling, with its complex 'matching rules', creates localized stresses where reaction-diffusion patterns break symmetry, forming irregular or 'glitched' structures within the ordered framework.
items.prompt: Create 8-12 distinct glyphs. Each glyph incorporates elements of the Trilobite-Sphinx tiling. Where the complex matching rules of the tiling would typically enforce conformity, reaction-diffusion processes introduce localized deviations – broad, flat black shape 'glitches' or irregular expansions that subtly disrupt the strict aperiodic order. Pure 2D silhouettes, black on white.
items.why_weird: The inherent complexity and self-imposed constraints (matching rules) of the Trilobite-Sphinx tiling are a fertile ground for reaction-diffusion to exploit subtle parameter gradients, leading to localized 'errors' in the pattern that highlight the underlying order.
items.fusion_logic: The matching rules and pairwise structure of the Trilobite-Sphinx tiling are used to create localized regions of high 'stress' or parameter inhomogeneity. Reaction-diffusion then exploits these inhomogeneities to generate asymmetric or 'glitched' patterns at these specific interfaces.

source_dna.quasicrystals: Uses the complex matching rules and paired nature of the Trilobite-Sphinx tiling to create localized conditions for symmetry breaking.
source_dna.reaction_diffusion: Generates irregular or 'glitched' pattern formations at specific interfaces dictated by the tiling's matching rules, introducing localized asymmetry.

items.title: Quasicrystal Diffraction Pattern Bloom
items.basis: The sharp, intense diffraction spots of quasicrystals are modeled as seeds for reaction-diffusion 'blooms' that spread outwards, their intensity modulated by the quasiperiodic wavevector positions.
items.prompt: Design 6-10 unique glyphs. Each glyph represents a stylized quasicrystal diffraction pattern, depicted as a dense arrangement of broad black spots (representing intense peaks). From the centers of these prominent spots, reaction-diffusion 'blooms' of flat black shape spread outwards, forming organic, yet structured, silhouettes. The overall composition must evoke the stark purity of diffraction data, black on white, 2D.
items.why_weird: This fuses the abstract, mathematical concept of diffraction intensity with the physical process of pattern growth, creating forms that are both crystalline in their origin and organic in their manifestation.
items.fusion_logic: The positions and relative intensities of quasicrystal diffraction peaks are used as initial conditions (seeds) for reaction-diffusion simulations. The subsequent growth and spread of these reaction-diffusion patterns ('blooms') are influenced by the quasiperiodic structure, creating forms that are sharp at their origin but organically diffuse outwards.

source_dna.quasicrystals: Uses the quasiperiodic positions of diffraction peaks as seeding points for reaction-diffusion growth.
source_dna.reaction_diffusion: Generates expanding 'blooms' or wave-fronts originating from diffraction peak locations, whose spread is implicitly guided by the underlying quasiperiodic order.

items.title: Golden Ratio Spiral Growth Fronts
items.basis: Reaction-diffusion fronts are guided by the golden ratio (phi) spiral, a common motif in quasicrystal geometry. The growth follows a path dictated by phi, creating spiraling patterns within the broad silhouette style.
items.prompt: Create 7-9 distinct glyphs. Each glyph features a prominent golden ratio spiral as a central motif. Reaction-diffusion patterns manifest as broad, flat black bands that follow this spiral path, often leaving an open center. The patterns should appear as if growing outwards or inwards along the spiral. Pure 2D, black shapes on a white background, strong negative space.
items.why_weird: This forces a dynamic, emergent process (reaction-diffusion) to strictly adhere to a specific irrational geometric construction (golden spiral), linking growth dynamics to fundamental quasicrystalline ratios.
items.fusion_logic: The golden ratio spiral is used to define the primary path and curvature for reaction-diffusion fronts. Parameters are tuned such that the wave-like patterns propagate along this spiral, creating large, open, spiraling structures that embody both the irrationality of phi and the spatial dynamics of diffusion.

source_dna.quasicrystals: Employs the golden ratio (phi) and associated spiral formations as the guiding geometry for pattern propagation.
source_dna.reaction_diffusion: Generates large-scale, open-centered spiral patterns by having reaction-diffusion fronts follow a trajectory defined by the golden ratio.
